docs.title: MedAnvil
docs.text:
Train, deploy, and monitor medical imaging AI — from your browser.

Research Use Only

This platform is intended for research and development of medical imaging AI models. Model outputs must not be used as the sole basis for clinical decisions without review by qualified healthcare professionals. Clinical deployment requires regulatory approval (e.g. FDA clearance), clinical validation studies, and human-in-the-loop oversight.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Feature Description 🏋️ Train Classification & segmentation on SageMaker (ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNet, ViT, SegResNet, SwinUNETR) with MLflow tracking 🚀 Deploy One-click deployment to real-time or async SageMaker endpoints 🔬 Invoke Test endpoints from the UI — DICOM, NIfTI, S3 URIs, or local files 📊 Evaluate Run evaluation jobs against deployed endpoints with per-class metrics, confusion matrices, and ROC curves 📈 Monitor Data capture, data quality baselines, and drift detection schedules via SageMaker Model Monitor ⚖️ Fairness Scan DICOM metadata for demographic distributions and bias auditing 📝 Report Generate structured paper sections (abstract, methods, results, discussion) from completed jobs 🔄 Fine-tune Resume training from checkpoints with full lineage tracking

docs.title: Responsible AI
docs.text:
This platform processes medical imaging data for AI model training and evaluation. Important considerations:

  • Not a medical device — AI outputs are for research purposes only and must not be used as the sole basis for clinical decisions.
  • Human oversight required — Any clinical deployment requires qualified healthcare professional review of all AI predictions.
  • Regulatory compliance — Production medical AI systems require appropriate regulatory clearances (FDA, CE marking) and institutional review board approval.
  • Fairness and bias — Use the built-in Fairness Analysis feature to audit demographic representation in training data. Monitor model performance across subgroups.
  • Validation — Models must undergo clinical validation studies before use in patient care settings.
  • Data privacy — Ensure compliance with HIPAA, GDPR, and applicable data protection regulations when handling patient data.

Built with MONAI · Powered by AWS SageMaker

  "image_uri": "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-classification:latest",
  "role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerRole",
  "instance_type": "ml.m5.xlarge",
  "instance_count": 1,
  "inference_script": "inference.py",
  "environment": {},
  "async_endpoint": false,
  "output_s3_uri": null,
  "max_concurrent": 10,
  "enable_data_capture": false,
  "capture_s3_uri": null,
  "capture_sampling_pct": 100
}

Field Default Notes model_artifacts — Omit to import/track an existing endpoint by name only image_uri — Required when deploying a new endpoint role_arn — Required when deploying a new endpoint async_endpoint false Set true for async inference; output_s3_uri required enable_data_capture false Enable capture at creation time capture_sampling_pct 100 1–100

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
⚠️ Research Use Only — Models trained and deployed through this platform are for research and development purposes. Clinical deployment requires regulatory review, validation against clinical standards, and human oversight. AI predictions must not be used as the sole basis for medical decisions.

This document covers all configuration options for the MedML Training Dashboard — environment files, AWS credentials, Docker setup, IAM permissions, and ECR image management.

docs.title: 1. Environment Files
docs.text:
The application uses a two-layer environment variable system loaded by python-dotenv in main.py:

File Purpose Committed to git? .env General application config (region, MLflow URI, log settings) Yes (.env.example template) .env.local Account-specific secrets and identifiers (account ID, role ARN, ECR URIs) No (gitignored) .env.local.example Template for .env.local with placeholder values Yes

Load order: .env is loaded first, then .env.local overrides any overlapping keys:

load_dotenv()                          # loads .env
load_dotenv(".env.local", override=True)  # loads .env.local, overriding duplicates

docs.title: Initial setup
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
cp .env.local.example .env.local
# Edit .env.local with your real AWS account ID, role ARN, and ECR URIs

docs.title: 2. General Config (.env)
docs.text:
These variables control application behavior and third-party service endpoints.

Variable Description Default Example AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS access key (optional if using ~/.aws/credentials or IAM roles) — AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS secret key — wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY AWS_DEFAULT_REGION AWS region for all boto3 clients us-east-1 us-west-2 MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI MLflow server endpoint for experiment tracking http://localhost:5000 http://mlflow.internal:5000 MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_NAME Default MLflow experiment name medical_imaging_experiments spine-classification-v2 TENSORBOARD_LOG_DIR Directory for TensorBoard event files ./logs/tensorboard /data/tb-logs DEBUG Enable debug mode (verbose logging, auto-reload) True False LOG_LEVEL Python logging level INFO DEBUG, WARNING, ERROR

docs.title: Example .env
docs.text:
# AWS Configuration (optional — can be configured via UI)
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_access_key_here
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret_key_here
AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1

# MLflow Configuration
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://localhost:5000
MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_NAME=medical_imaging_experiments

# TensorBoard Configuration
TENSORBOARD_LOG_DIR=./logs/tensorboard

# Application Configuration
DEBUG=True
LOG_LEVEL=INFO

docs.title: 3. Account-Specific Config (.env.local)
docs.text:
These variables are unique to your AWS account and should never be committed.

Variable Description Example AWS_ACCOUNT_ID Your 12-digit AWS account ID 123456789012 SAGEMAKER_ROLE_ARN SageMaker execution role ARN arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm TRAINING_IMAGE_CLASSIFICATION ECR URI for the classification training container 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-training-byoc-classification:latest TRAINING_IMAGE_SEGMENTATION ECR URI for the segmentation training container 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-training-byoc-segmentation:latest INFERENCE_IMAGE_CLASSIFICATION ECR URI for the classification inference container 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-classification:latest INFERENCE_IMAGE_SEGMENTATION ECR URI for the segmentation inference container 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-segmentation:latest DEFAULT_DATA_S3_URI Default training data S3 URI (pre-populates the UI form) s3://<your-bucket-name>/training/spine-xr/ TEST_IMAGE_S3_URI S3 URI of a test DICOM image for integration tests s3://<your-bucket-name>/test/sample.dcm TEST_SEGMENTATION_S3_URI S3 URI of a test NIfTI volume for segmentation tests s3://<your-bucket-name>/test/volume.nii.gz

docs.title: 4. AWS Credentials
docs.text: The application supports three methods for providing AWS credentials, checked in this order:

docs.title: Method 1: Environment variables (.env or .env.local)
docs.text:
Set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in your .env file:

AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1

Best for: local development when you don't have AWS CLI configured.

docs.title: Method 2: AWS credentials file (~/.aws/credentials)
docs.text:
Configure the AWS CLI and the app picks up the default profile automatically:

aws configure
# Enter: Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Region, Output format

Or use a named profile by setting AWS_PROFILE:

export AWS_PROFILE=medml-dev
python main.py

Best for: developers who use multiple AWS accounts.

docs.title: Method 3: Dashboard UI
docs.text:
Navigate to the AWS tab in the dashboard and enter credentials interactively. The dashboard calls AWSService.configure_credentials() which creates boto3 clients in memory — credentials are not persisted to disk.

Best for: quick testing or demos without touching local config files.

docs.title: Credential priority
docs.text: If environment variables are set at startup, the AWSService automatically initializes boto3 clients. If they're absent, the service remains unconfigured until credentials are provided via the UI.

docs.title: 5. Runtime Config API
docs.text: The GET /api/config endpoint serves non-secret configuration values to the frontend, allowing the UI to pre-populate forms with ECR URIs, role ARNs, and default data paths.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "aws_account_id": "123456789012",
  "aws_region": "us-east-1",
  "sagemaker_role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm",
  "training_image_classification": "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-training-byoc-classification:latest",
  "training_image_segmentation": "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-training-byoc-segmentation:latest",
  "inference_image_classification": "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-classification:latest",
  "inference_image_segmentation": "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-segmentation:latest",
  "default_data_s3_uri": "s3://<your-bucket-name>/training/spine-xr/"
}

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Values come from environment variables (loaded from .env.local)
  • If AWS_ACCOUNT_ID is set but specific image URIs are not, the endpoint auto-generates ECR URIs using the conventional naming scheme
  • No secrets (access keys, secret keys) are ever exposed through this endpoint

docs.title: Frontend usage
docs.text:
The dashboard JavaScript fetches /api/config on page load to pre-fill the SageMaker training form:

const config = await fetch('/api/config').then(r => r.json());
document.getElementById('image-uri').value = config.training_image_classification;
document.getElementById('role-arn').value = config.sagemaker_role_arn;

docs.title: docker-compose.yml
docs.text:
The single-container setup runs FastAPI, MLflow, and TensorBoard together:

version: '3.8'

services:
  medml-platform:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"  # FastAPI application
      - "5000:5000"  # MLflow
      - "6006:6006"  # TensorBoard
    environment:

      - ./data:/app/data
      - ./logs:/app/logs
      - ./models:/app/models
    restart: unless-stopped

docs.text:
Pass AWS credentials and account config at run time (never bake them into the image):

docker-compose run -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID \
                   -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY \

# docker-compose.override.yml
services:

docs.title: 7. SageMaker IAM Role
docs.text: The SAGEMAKER_ROLE_ARN must have permissions to run training jobs, deploy endpoints, access S3 data, pull ECR images, write logs, and track experiments with MLflow.

docs.title: Role creation script
docs.text:
The create-sagemaker-role.sh script is the bash equivalent of the shared Python get_or_create_role() utility (found in utils.py). It creates a role with managed AWS policies and an inline MLflow policy.

# Create with the default role name (AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm)
./create-sagemaker-role.sh

# Or specify a custom role name
./create-sagemaker-role.sh MyCustomRoleName

The script also runs via the setup helper:

./setup.sh --role

If the role already exists, the script updates the trust policy and re-attaches all policies (idempotent).

docs.title: Default role name
docs.text:
AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm

This matches the Python get_or_create_role() default, so both the bash script and Python notebooks produce the same role.

docs.title: Trust policy
docs.text:
The role trusts the SageMaker service to assume it:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Service": "sagemaker.amazonaws.com"
      },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Managed policies attached
docs.text:
The script attaches the following AWS managed policies:

Policy Purpose AmazonSageMakerFullAccess Training jobs, endpoints, processing, monitoring AmazonS3FullAccess Read/write training data, model artifacts, capture logs AmazonRekognitionFullAccess Image analysis capabilities ComprehendFullAccess NLP text analysis ComprehendMedicalFullAccess Medical text extraction AmazonElasticContainerRegistryPublicFullAccess Pull/push container images AmazonSageMakerCanvasFullAccess SageMaker Canvas no-code ML AmazonSageMakerCanvasAIServicesAccess Canvas AI services integration AmazonSageMakerCanvasSMDataScienceAssistantAccess Canvas data science assistant AmazonSageMakerCanvasDataPrepFullAccess Canvas data preparation

Production note: For production deployments, replace FullAccess policies with scoped policies restricted to specific bucket ARNs, repository ARNs, and resource prefixes. The broad policies above are suitable for development and experimentation.

docs.title: Inline MLflow policy
docs.text:
An inline policy named mlflow-policy is added for SageMaker MLflow experiment tracking. The resource is scoped to your specific tracking server:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "MLflowTrackingAccess",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["sagemaker-mlflow:*"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:sagemaker:<region>:<account-id>:mlflow-tracking-server/<server-name>"
    }
  ]
}

The script determines the resource ARN based on your .env.local configuration:

MLFLOW_TRACKING_SERVER_NAME set? AWS_ACCOUNT_ID set? Resource scope Yes Yes arn:aws:sagemaker:REGION:ACCOUNT:mlflow-tracking-server/SERVER-NAME No Yes arn:aws:sagemaker:REGION:ACCOUNT:mlflow-tracking-server/* (all servers in account) No No arn:aws:sagemaker:REGION:*:mlflow-tracking-server/* (fallback)

Security note: Always set MLFLOW_TRACKING_SERVER_NAME in .env.local to scope permissions to your specific tracking server. Using Resource: "*" grants MLflow permissions across all tracking servers in the account.

docs.title: When to use which approach
docs.text: Context Method Running outside SageMaker (EC2, local, CI/CD) ./create-sagemaker-role.sh or Python get_or_create_role() Running inside SageMaker (Studio, notebook instances) sagemaker.get_execution_role() — retrieves the pre-assigned role from instance metadata

docs.title: Creating the role manually
docs.text:
If you prefer not to use the script:

# 1. Create the role with trust policy
aws iam create-role \
  --role-name AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm \
  --assume-role-policy-document file://trust-policy.json \
  --description "SageMaker execution role for medical imaging training"

# 2. Attach managed policies
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm \
  --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSageMakerFullAccess
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm \
  --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3FullAccess
# ... (attach remaining policies as listed above)

# 3. Add inline MLflow policy
aws iam put-role-policy \
  --role-name AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm \
  --policy-name mlflow-policy \
  --policy-document file://mlflow-policy.json

docs.title: After role creation
docs.text:
The script automatically updates SAGEMAKER_ROLE_ARN in .env.local. If you created the role manually, update it yourself:

# In .env.local
SAGEMAKER_ROLE_ARN=arn:aws:iam::<your-account-id>:role/AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm

docs.title: 8. ECR Repositories
docs.text: Four ECR repositories are required — two for training (classification + segmentation) and two for inference.

docs.title: Repository names
docs.text: Repository Purpose Build script sm-training-byoc-classification Classification training container build_and_push.sh sm-training-byoc-segmentation Segmentation training container build_and_push.sh sm-inference-byoc-classification Classification inference container build_and_push_inference.sh sm-inference-byoc-segmentation Segmentation inference container build_and_push_inference.sh

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Docker installed and running
  2. AWS CLI configured with ECR push permissions
  3. Login to the AWS Deep Learning Containers registry (base image source):
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin \
    763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

This is required on every new machine. Without it, Docker cannot pull the PyTorch base image and the build fails with 403 Forbidden.

docs.title: Build and push commands
docs.text:
# All images at once (recommended)
./setup.sh --images

# Or individually:

# Classification training image
./build_and_push.sh classification

# Segmentation training image
./build_and_push.sh segmentation

# Classification inference image
./build_and_push_inference.sh classification

# Segmentation inference image
./build_and_push_inference.sh segmentation

# Force full rebuild (no Docker layer cache)
./build_and_push.sh classification --no-cache
./build_and_push_inference.sh segmentation --no-cache

All scripts read AWS_ACCOUNT_ID and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION from .env.local. Builds use Docker's layer cache by default for speed; pass --no-cache when base images or dependencies have changed.

Each script automatically: 1. Logs in to the AWS DLC ECR registry (for pulling the base image) 2. Builds the Docker image from the appropriate Dockerfile 3. Logs into your ECR registry 4. Creates the repository if it doesn't exist 5. Pushes the image

The inference build script (build_and_push_inference.sh) additionally deletes the existing ECR image before pushing and verifies that the pushed manifest is in Docker V2 format (required by SageMaker's CreateModel API).

Important: Docker manifest format — SageMaker only supports Docker V2 manifests (application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json). Newer versions of Docker with BuildKit enabled produce OCI format images by default, which SageMaker rejects with Unsupported manifest media type application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json. The build scripts handle this automatically by using DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0, which forces Docker V2 output. If you build images manually, always include DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 in your build command.

Note: SageMaker's CreateModel operation (used for inference/deployment) is stricter about manifest formats than CreateTrainingJob. You may find that training images built with OCI manifests work fine, but the same format fails at deployment time. Always use Docker V2 manifests for both training and inference images to avoid surprises.

docs.title: Debugging: OCI Manifest Errors
docs.text:
If you encounter Unsupported manifest media type application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json when deploying, follow these steps:

1. Verify the manifest type in ECR:

aws ecr batch-get-image \
  --repository-name sm-inference-byoc-classification \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --image-ids imageTag=latest \
  --query 'images[0].imageManifestMediaType' \
  --output text

Expected: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json Problem: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json

2. Why this happens:

  • Docker 23+ uses BuildKit by default, which outputs OCI format images
  • SageMaker's CreateModel API (inference/deployment) validates the manifest type and rejects OCI
  • SageMaker's CreateTrainingJob API does not perform this check — training images with OCI manifests work fine because the container runtime (containerd) on training instances supports both formats
  • This inconsistency means the same build process can produce images that work for training but fail at deployment

3. Fix — delete from ECR, rebuild, and push:

The working solution requires three things: clearing the Docker cache, deleting the old image from ECR, and rebuilding with BuildKit disabled.

# Clear all cached images (removes OCI-format base image layers)
docker system prune -a --force

# Login to DLC registry (for pulling the base image)
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

# Delete the existing OCI image from ECR
aws ecr batch-delete-image \
  --repository-name sm-inference-byoc-classification \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --image-ids imageTag=latest

# Rebuild with BuildKit disabled and no cache
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 docker build --no-cache --platform linux/amd64 \
  -f Dockerfile.inference --build-arg TASK=classification \
  -t 811260109607.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-classification:latest .

# Login to your ECR
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 811260109607.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

# Push fresh
docker push 811260109607.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-classification:latest

# Verify — must return application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json
aws ecr batch-get-image \
  --repository-name sm-inference-byoc-classification \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --image-ids imageTag=latest \
  --query 'images[0].imageManifest' --output text \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.loads(sys.stdin.read()).get('mediaType','unknown'))"

All three steps are critical: - docker system prune -a — Without this, Docker reuses cached OCI-format base image layers even with --no-cache - Delete from ECR — Pushing with the same tag doesn't always overwrite the manifest - DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 — Forces the legacy builder which outputs Docker V2 format

4. If the above still produces OCI manifests:

Configure the Docker daemon to disable OCI output entirely:

sudo tee /etc/docker/daemon.json <<'EOF'
{
  "features": {
    "containerd-snapshotter": false
  }
}
EOF
sudo systemctl restart docker

Then repeat step 3. This ensures Docker never converts back to OCI on push.

5. References:

  • AWS re:Post — OCI format unsupported when creating a SageMaker model
  • AWS re:Post — Manifest error when staging ML model
  • Stack Overflow — Error when using CreateModel for SageMaker
  • MLflow GitHub Issue #13834 — Unsupported manifest media type
  • AWS re:Post — SageMaker Docker OCI manifests support (feature request)

docs.title: Custom Model Workflow
docs.text:
⚠️ Research Use Only — Models trained and deployed through this platform are for research and development purposes. Clinical deployment requires regulatory review, validation against clinical standards, and human oversight. AI predictions must not be used as the sole basis for medical decisions.

A guide for AI researchers who want to add custom models to the MedML Training Dashboard without modifying the backend code.

docs.title: What You Provide (Zip File)
docs.text:
my-model-name.zip
├── model_def.py              # REQUIRED — architecture + MODELS registry
├── inference.py              # OPTIONAL — custom serving hooks (defaults to built-in)
├── train.py                  # OPTIONAL — custom training loop (defaults to built-in)
├── requirements.txt          # OPTIONAL — extra pip packages for training
└── sample_config.json        # OPTIONAL — suggested hyperparameters

docs.title: The Key Contract: model_def.py
docs.text:
Your model_def.py must have: 1. A MODELS dict that registers your model(s) with metadata 2. A get_model(model_name, num_classes, **kwargs) function that returns an instantiated PyTorch model

"""
Custom model: Cardiac Attention UNet
"""
import torch.nn as nn

# This dict makes the model appear in the dashboard dropdown under "Custom Models"
MODELS = {
    "cardiac-attention-unet": {
        "description": "Attention UNet for cardiac MRI segmentation",
        "parameters": "4.2M",
        "input_size": "128x128x64",
        "pretrained": False,
        "task": "segmentation",       # "classification" or "segmentation"
        "dimension": "3D",            # "2D" or "3D"
    }
}

def get_model(model_name, num_classes=1, **kwargs):
    """Called by train.py and inference.py to instantiate the model."""
    if model_name == "cardiac-attention-unet":
        return CardiacAttentionUNet(in_channels=1, out_channels=num_classes)
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown model: {model_name}")


class CardiacAttentionUNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels=1, out_channels=1):
        super().__init__()
        # ... your architecture here ...

    def forward(self, x):
        # ...
        return x

docs.title: MODELS Dict Fields
docs.text: Field Required Description description yes Human-readable description parameters yes Approximate parameter count (e.g. "4.2M") input_size yes Expected input dimensions (e.g. "128x128x64") pretrained yes Whether pretrained weights are used (True/False) task yes "classification" or "segmentation" dimension yes "2D" or "3D"

docs.title: Step-by-Step Workflow
docs.text: Step Action What happens 1 Upload zip via Training tab → "Upload Custom Model" Extracted to data/custom_models/<model_name>/; model appears in dropdown under "Custom Models" 2 Select model from dropdown, fill training form, click Train SageMaker job uses the custom source_dir; train.py imports get_model() from your model_def.py 3 Job completes model.tar.gz bundles: weights + model_def.py + inference.py + result.json 4 Click Deploy on the completed job Inference container loads model_def.py from artifact dynamically 5 Run Inference model_fn() imports your model_def.py from the model artifact 6 Run Evaluation Invokes the endpoint — works with any deployed model 7 Enable Monitoring Captures I/O — works unchanged for any endpoint

docs.title: inference.py (custom serving hooks)
docs.text:
Only needed if your model requires: - Custom input preprocessing (different from DICOM/NIfTI → tensor) - Custom output format (different from predictions/class/confidence) - Additional post-processing steps

If omitted, the built-in inference script handles: - Classification: DICOM/PNG/JPG → resize → normalize → softmax → class probabilities - Segmentation: NIfTI → resize to 128x128x64 → sigmoid → binary mask

docs.title: train.py (custom training loop)
docs.text:
Only needed if your model requires: - Custom loss function - Custom data loading/augmentation - Multi-stage training - Special optimizer configuration

If omitted, the built-in train.py handles: - Data loading from S3 (class folders for classification, subject folders for segmentation) - Standard training loop with validation - Checkpoint saving (best model by validation metric) - MLflow logging (when MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is set)

docs.title: requirements.txt (extra dependencies)
docs.text: List any packages not already in the BYOC training container. Pre-installed packages include: - torch, torchvision - monai - nibabel, SimpleITK, pydicom, itk - mlflow, tensorboard - tqdm

docs.title: Example: Adding a 3D ResNet for Classification
docs.text:
# model_def.py
from monai.networks.nets import ResNet

MODELS = {
    "resnet3d-18": {
        "description": "3D ResNet-18 for volumetric classification",
        "parameters": "33M",
        "input_size": "64x64x64",
        "pretrained": False,
        "task": "classification",
        "dimension": "3D",
    }
}

def get_model(model_name, num_classes=8, **kwargs):
    if model_name == "resnet3d-18":
        return ResNet(
            block="basic",
            layers=[2, 2, 2, 2],
            block_inplanes=[64, 128, 256, 512],
            spatial_dims=3,
            n_input_channels=1,
            num_classes=num_classes,
        )
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown model: {model_name}")

Then zip it: 

zip resnet3d-18.zip model_def.py

Upload via the dashboard, select "resnet3d-18" from the model dropdown, and train.

docs.title: Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide covers building the Docker images required for SageMaker training and inference, setting up ECR repositories, and deploying the MedML dashboard itself.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker installed and running
  • AWS CLI v2 configured with credentials that have ECR push/pull permissions
  • An AWS account with SageMaker, ECR, and S3 access
  • Python 3.11+ (for local dashboard development)

docs.title: Docker Image Architecture
docs.text:
The project uses three Docker images:

Image Purpose Dockerfile ECR Repository Training (Classification) SageMaker BYOC training container Dockerfile.sagemaker sm-training-byoc-classification Training (Segmentation) SageMaker BYOC training container Dockerfile.sagemaker sm-training-byoc-segmentation Inference (Classification) SageMaker real-time/async endpoint Dockerfile.inference sm-inference-byoc-classification Inference (Segmentation) SageMaker real-time/async endpoint Dockerfile.inference sm-inference-byoc-segmentation Dashboard FastAPI web application Dockerfile — (local/ECS)

docs.title: ECR Repository Setup
docs.text:
Create the ECR repositories before your first build:

AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=123456789012
AWS_REGION=us-east-1

for repo in sm-training-byoc-classification sm-training-byoc-segmentation \
            sm-inference-byoc-classification sm-inference-byoc-segmentation; do
  aws ecr create-repository \
    --repository-name "$repo" \
    --region "$AWS_REGION" \
    --image-scanning-configuration scanOnPush=true
done

The build scripts also create repositories automatically if they don't exist, but pre-creating them allows you to configure scanning and lifecycle policies.

docs.title: Base Image Authentication
docs.text:
The training and inference Dockerfiles pull from the AWS Deep Learning Containers registry (763104351884.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com). You must authenticate before building:

aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin \
    763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

This is required once per machine (or after token expiry). Without it, the build fails with 403 Forbidden.

docs.title: Training image
docs.text:
The training container uses the PyTorch Training DLC:

FROM 763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/pytorch-training:2.9.0-gpu-py312-cu130-ubuntu22.04-sagemaker

If this tag is unavailable in your region, find alternatives:

aws ecr describe-images \
  --registry-id 763104351884 \
  --repository-name pytorch-training \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --query 'imageDetails[*].imageTags' \
  --output text | tr '\t' '\n' | grep "py312" | sort

A known working alternative: 

763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/pytorch-training:2.6.0-gpu-py312-cu124-ubuntu22.04-sagemaker

docs.title: Inference image
docs.text:
The inference container uses the PyTorch Inference DLC:

FROM 763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/pytorch-inference:2.6.0-gpu-py312-cu124-ubuntu22.04-sagemaker

This provides the serve entrypoint, nginx, gunicorn, and the multi-model server required by SageMaker endpoints.

docs.title: Using setup.sh (recommended)
docs.text:
The easiest way to build and push all images is the unified setup script:

./setup.sh --images

This builds and pushes all four images (training + inference, classification + segmentation), reading AWS_ACCOUNT_ID and region from .env.local.

docs.title: Using build_and_push.sh
docs.text:
To build a single training image:

# Classification training image
./build_and_push.sh classification

# Segmentation training image
./build_and_push.sh segmentation

# Full rebuild without Docker cache
./build_and_push.sh classification --no-cache

The script reads AWS_ACCOUNT_ID and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION from .env.local. No positional arguments for account ID or region are needed.

By default, builds use Docker's layer cache for faster rebuilds. Pass --no-cache to force a full rebuild (useful when base image or dependencies have changed).

What it does: 1. Logs in to the AWS DLC ECR registry (base image source) 2. Builds the Docker image from Dockerfile.sagemaker with the TASK build arg 3. Logs in to your ECR registry 4. Creates the repository if it doesn't exist 5. Pushes the image

Files bundled into the image: - src/<task>/requirements.txt — pip dependencies - src/<task>/ — all training scripts (train.py, model_def.py, etc.)

The resulting image tag: <account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/sm-training-byoc-<task>:latest

docs.title: Dockerfile.sagemaker structure
docs.text:
ARG TASK=classification
FROM 763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/pytorch-training:2.9.0-gpu-py312-cu130-ubuntu22.04-sagemaker
ARG TASK
COPY src/${TASK}/requirements.txt /tmp/requirements.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /tmp/requirements.txt
COPY src/${TASK}/ /opt/program/
COPY src/inference/${TASK}/ /opt/program/inference/
ENV SAGEMAKER_PROGRAM train.py

Notes: - SageMaker training containers require root (no USER directive) - No HEALTHCHECK — SageMaker manages container lifecycle - The SAGEMAKER_PROGRAM env var tells SageMaker which script to execute - The src/inference/${TASK}/ directory is included so training scripts can copy inference artifacts (e.g., inference.py) into model_dir/code/ for SageMaker PyTorch serving

docs.title: Using build_and_push_inference.sh
docs.text:
# Classification inference image
./build_and_push_inference.sh classification

# Segmentation inference image
./build_and_push_inference.sh segmentation

# Full rebuild without Docker cache
./build_and_push_inference.sh classification --no-cache

The script reads AWS_ACCOUNT_ID and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION from .env.local.

By default, builds use Docker's layer cache. Pass --no-cache for a full rebuild.

What it does: 1. Logs in to the AWS DLC ECR registry (base image source) 2. Builds the Docker image from Dockerfile.inference with the TASK build arg 3. Logs in to your ECR registry 4. Creates the repository if it doesn't exist 5. Deletes the existing latest image from ECR (ensures the new push fully replaces the old manifest) 6. Pushes the new image 7. Verifies the pushed manifest format is Docker V2 (not OCI) — SageMaker's CreateModel API rejects OCI manifests

docs.title: Dockerfile.inference structure
docs.text:
ARG TASK=classification
FROM 763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/pytorch-inference:2.6.0-gpu-py312-cu124-ubuntu22.04-sagemaker
ARG TASK
COPY src/inference/${TASK}/requirements.txt /tmp/requirements-inference.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /tmp/requirements-inference.txt

Notes: - SAGEMAKER_PROGRAM is set at deploy time via create_model Environment — not baked in - SageMaker inference containers require root for nginx/gunicorn - The inference script (inference.py) is bundled inside model.tar.gz, not the container image

docs.title: model.tar.gz Structure
docs.text:
SageMaker's PyTorch serving container requires inference code to be located at code/inference.py inside the model archive. The training scripts now automatically copy inference artifacts to the correct location (model_dir/code/).

Required structure:

model.tar.gz
├── best_model.pth          # Model weights
├── result.json             # Training metadata
└── code/
    └── inference.py        # Inference handler (model_fn, input_fn, predict_fn, output_fn)

Important: Placing inference.py at the root of the archive will not work with the SageMaker PyTorch serving container. It must be under code/.

docs.title: Repackaging Existing Models
docs.text:
If you have an existing model.tar.gz that was created before this change (with inference.py at the root), use the repackaging script:

python tests/integration/repackage_model.py s3://your-bucket/output/job-name/output/model.tar.gz

This downloads the archive, restructures it to place inference artifacts under code/, and re-uploads it to the same S3 location.

Starts MLflow, TensorBoard, and the FastAPI app together in a single terminal.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
All account-specific configuration goes in .env.local (gitignored): - AWS_ACCOUNT_ID - SAGEMAKER_ROLE_ARN - ECR image URIs for training and inference - DEFAULT_DATA_S3_URI

See the Configuration page for the full list.

docs.title: Persistent state
docs.text:
The dashboard persists state to JSON files in data/: - data/sagemaker_jobs.json — training job records - data/deployments.json — endpoint deployment records - data/monitoring.json — Model Monitor schedule records - data/training_reports/ — per-job JSON reports

Ensure this directory is on persistent storage (e.g., EBS volume if running on EC2/ECS).

docs.title: AWS credentials
docs.text: For production, use an IAM instance profile or ECS task role rather than static credentials. The dashboard auto-detects credentials from the environment/instance metadata on startup.

docs.title: Reverse proxy
docs.text: For production deployments, put the dashboard behind a reverse proxy (nginx, ALB) with: - HTTPS termination - Authentication (e.g., Cognito, IAM Identity Center) - Rate limiting

docs.title: Instance sizing
docs.text: The dashboard itself is lightweight (FastAPI + Jinja2). A t3.small or equivalent is sufficient. The heavy compute (training, inference) happens on SageMaker instances, not the dashboard host.

docs.title: Transferring to Another Machine
docs.text:
The cleanest approach is git:

# Source machine
git add -A && git commit -m "your message" && git push origin <branch>

# Target machine
git clone <repo-url> && git checkout <branch>

Minimum files needed for the Docker build:

Dockerfile.inference
build_and_push.sh
build_and_push_inference.sh
src/classification/    (for classification images)
src/segmentation/      (for segmentation images)
src/inference/         (for inference images)

docs.title: 403 Forbidden during Docker build
docs.text:
You haven't authenticated to the AWS DLC ECR registry. Run: 

aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin \
    763104351884.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

docs.title: Image tag not found
docs.text:
The base image tag may not be available in your region. List available tags: 

aws ecr describe-images \
  --registry-id 763104351884 \
  --repository-name pytorch-training \
  --region <your-region> \
  --query 'imageDetails[*].imageTags' \
  --output text | tr '\t' '\n' | grep "py312" | sort

docs.title: SageMaker training job fails immediately
docs.text: Check: 1. The ECR image URI is correct and accessible by the SageMaker execution role 2. The execution role has permissions to pull from your ECR repository 3. The training data S3 URI is accessible by the role 4. The instance type is available in your region

docs.title: Endpoint creation stuck in Creating
docs.text: SageMaker endpoint creation typically takes 5–10 minutes. If it exceeds 15 minutes, check the SageMaker console for error details. Common causes: - Inference image doesn't have the serve entrypoint - model.tar.gz is missing required files or has incorrect structure (must contain code/inference.py and model weights) - Instance type capacity issues in the region

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
All Pydantic models and enums live in app/models/schemas.py. This includes: - Request models (e.g., AWSCredentials, SageMakerTrainingConfig, ModelImportRequest) - Response models (e.g., ImportedModel, TrainingJob) - Enums (e.g., ModelType, TaskType, DimensionType, JobStatus)

Router-local request models (e.g., EndpointDeployRequest, InferenceRequest) are defined in their respective router files when they are specific to that router only.

docs.title: Routers
docs.text:
• One file per API prefix (e.g., training_router.py → /api/training)
  • Import service instances from sibling routers when sharing state: 
    from app.routers.aws_router import aws_service
  • Each router creates its service instance(s) at module level
  • Routers handle HTTP concerns (status codes, exceptions) — business logic stays in services

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
• Plain Python classes, no FastAPI dependencies
  • Instantiated as module-level singletons in their respective router
  • AWSService is a shared singleton imported from aws_router
  • Always check s3_client is not None before use; raise ValueError("AWS credentials not configured") if not set
  • State persistence: services that persist data use _load() / _save() methods with JSON files in data/

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Services raise ValueError for bad input and FileNotFoundError for missing resources
  • Routers catch exceptions and convert to HTTPException:
  • ValueError → 400 Bad Request
  • FileNotFoundError / KeyError → 404 Not Found
  • General Exception → 500 Internal Server Error
  • Always log errors before re-raising: 
    except Exception as e:
    logger.error(f"Operation failed: {e}")
    raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Each module creates its own logger: 

import logging
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

Use appropriate levels: - logger.info() — successful operations, job starts - logger.warning() — recoverable issues, fallbacks - logger.error() — failures that result in error responses

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
• Loaded via python-dotenv in main.py (.env first, then .env.local with override)
  • Never hardcode credentials, account IDs, or bucket names
  • Access via os.environ.get("VAR_NAME", "default")

docs.title: Adding a New Model Architecture
docs.text:
1. Register in model_def.py — Add an entry to the MODELS dict in src/classification/model_def.py or src/segmentation/model_def.py:
MODELS = {
    # ... existing models ...
    "my_new_model": {
        "description": "My custom architecture",
        "parameters": "12.5M",
        "input_size": "224x224",
        "pretrained": True,
        "task": "classification",
        "dimension": "2D",
    },
}
  1. Implement the factory function — In the same model_def.py, add a case to the get_model() function:
def get_model(model_name, num_classes, pretrained=True):
    if model_name == "my_new_model":
        model = MyNewModel(num_classes=num_classes, pretrained=pretrained)
        return model
    # ... existing cases ...

  1. No router/service changes needed — The /api/training/models endpoint dynamically reads the MODELS dict via AST parsing.

  2. Rebuild the Docker image — If using SageMaker: 

    ./build_and_push.sh <ACCOUNT_ID> <REGION> classification

docs.title: Step 1: Define the schema (if needed)
docs.text:
Add request/response models to app/models/schemas.py:

class MyNewRequest(BaseModel):
    field_one: str
    field_two: int = 10

docs.title: Step 2: Add service logic
docs.text:
Create or extend a service in app/services/:

# app/services/my_service.py
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class MyService:
    def do_something(self, param: str) -> dict:
        if not param:
            raise ValueError("param is required")
        # business logic here
        return {"result": param}

docs.title: Step 3: Add the router endpoint
docs.text:
In the appropriate router file:

from app.services.my_service import MyService

my_service = MyService()

@router.post("/my-endpoint")
async def my_endpoint(request: MyNewRequest):
    try:
        result = my_service.do_something(request.field_one)
        return result
    except ValueError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Operation failed: {e}")
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))

docs.title: Step 4: Register the router (if new file)
docs.text:
In main.py:

from app.routers import my_router
app.include_router(my_router.router, prefix="/api/my-prefix", tags=["MyTag"])

docs.title: Step 5: Add tests
docs.text: Add a unit test in tests/unit/ with mocked AWS dependencies and an integration test if the endpoint calls AWS.

docs.title: Unit Tests (pytest + moto)
docs.text:
Unit tests mock AWS services using moto and test service/router logic in isolation.

# Run all tests
pytest

# Run with verbose output
pytest -v

# Run a specific test file
pytest tests/unit/test_training_service.py

# Run with coverage
coverage run -m pytest && coverage report

Test files live in tests/unit/. Shared fixtures are in tests/fixtures/mock_data.py.

Example test pattern:

import pytest
from moto import mock_s3
import boto3
from app.services.training_service import TrainingService

@mock_s3
def test_import_model():
    # Setup mock S3
    s3 = boto3.client("s3", region_name="us-east-1")
    s3.create_bucket(Bucket="test-bucket")
    s3.put_object(Bucket="test-bucket", Key="model.pth", Body=b"fake model")

    service = TrainingService()
    # ... test logic ...

docs.title: Integration Tests
docs.text: Integration tests hit real AWS resources and require valid credentials.

docs.title: Local inference tests
docs.text:
Test the inference pipeline directly (no SageMaker endpoint required):

pytest tests/integration/test_local_inference.py -v -s

Environment variables: - TEST_LOCAL_IMAGE — path to a test DICOM/PNG/JPG file - MODEL_DIR — directory containing a .pth checkpoint

docs.title: Endpoint inference tests
docs.text:
Test a live SageMaker endpoint:

pytest tests/integration/test_endpoint_inference.py -v -s

# Or use the convenience wrapper
./tests/integration/run_inference_tests.sh /path/to/image.dcm

Environment variables: - ENDPOINT_NAME — name of an InService endpoint - TEST_IMAGE_S3_URI — S3 URI of a test image - TEST_LOCAL_IMAGE — local file path (optional; generates synthetic if unset)

docs.title: Quick endpoint test (no pytest)
docs.text:
# Classification
python tests/integration/test_endpoint.py --endpoint my-endpoint --local /path/to/image.dcm

# Segmentation
python test_endpoint_segmentation.py --endpoint my-seg-endpoint \
    --s3-uri s3://bucket/volume.nii.gz

docs.title: CLI invocation utility
docs.text:
python tests/invoke_endpoint.py --image /path/to/image.dcm --endpoint my-endpoint
python tests/invoke_endpoint.py --s3-uri s3://bucket/image.dcm --output result.json

docs.title: Pre-commit Hook for Secret Detection
docs.text:
Install the pre-commit hook to block commits containing account-specific values:

cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit
chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

The hook checks staged changes for: - Hardcoded AWS account IDs - Account-specific S3 bucket names - IAM Role ARNs (excluding test fixture account 123456789012) - AWS access key patterns (AKIA...)

If any are detected, the commit is blocked with a descriptive error message.

docs.title: CI/CD Workflow (scrub-check)
docs.text:
The .github/workflows/scrub-check.yml GitHub Actions workflow runs on every PR to main and performs the same checks as the pre-commit hook across the entire codebase:

  1. Hardcoded AWS account IDs — scans .py, .js, .html, .sh, .md, .yml, .yaml, .json files
  2. Hardcoded IAM Role ARNs — matches arn:aws:iam::<12-digit>:role/ patterns
  3. Account-specific S3 buckets — checks for known bucket name patterns
  4. Leaked secrets — detects AWS access key patterns (AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16})

The workflow excludes the .github/ directory itself from scanning.

docs.title: Frontend XSS Prevention (escapeHtml)
docs.text:
All user-supplied or API-returned data rendered in the DOM is passed through the escapeHtml() function defined in static/js/main.js:

function escapeHtml(str) {
    // Escapes <, >, &, ", ' to prevent XSS
}

This is used consistently across all frontend JavaScript files (training.js, deployment.js, evaluation.js, monitoring.js, inference.js, fairness.js, data.js).

docs.title: Subresource Integrity (SRI)
docs.text:
External CDN resources include integrity attributes and crossorigin="anonymous":

<link href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/6.0.0/css/all.min.css"
      rel="stylesheet"
      integrity="sha384-3B6NwesSXE7YJlcLI9RpRqGf2p/EgVH8BgoKTaUrmKNDkHPStTQ3EyoYjCGXaOTS"
      crossorigin="anonymous">

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4.4.0/dist/chart.umd.min.js"
        integrity="sha384-e6nUZLBkQ86NJ6TVVKAeSaK8jWa3NhkYWZFomE39AvDbQWeie9PlQqM3pmYW5d1g"
        crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

This ensures CDN-served files haven't been tampered with.

docs.title: No Hardcoded Credentials
docs.text:
• AWS credentials are loaded from environment variables or instance profiles
  • Account-specific config lives in .env.local (gitignored)
  • The scrub-check CI workflow and pre-commit hook enforce this at commit and PR time
  • Use <YOUR_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID> or 123456789012 as placeholders in documentation and examples

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Note: All http://localhost URLs in this documentation refer to the local development server and are not exposed to the public internet.

This guide walks you through setting up and running the MedML Training Dashboard — a FastAPI web application for managing medical image classification and segmentation workflows on AWS.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin, ensure you have the following:

Requirement Details Python 3.11 or higher AWS Account With permissions for S3, SageMaker, and ECR AWS CLI Installed and configured (~/.aws/credentials or environment variables) Docker Optional — required only for the multi-service setup (dashboard + MLflow + TensorBoard) Git For cloning the repository

docs.title: AWS Permissions
docs.text: Your AWS credentials need access to: - S3 — read/write for training data, model artifacts, and capture logs - SageMaker — create/manage training jobs, endpoints, processing jobs, and monitoring schedules - ECR — pull/push Docker images (only needed if building custom training containers)

docs.title: ⚠️ Medical AI Safety Notice
docs.text:
This platform is designed for research and development purposes only.

Models trained and deployed through this system are not validated for clinical use. Production deployment of medical imaging AI requires:

  1. Regulatory clearance — FDA 510(k), De Novo, PMA, CE marking, or equivalent regulatory pathway for your jurisdiction
  2. Clinical validation studies — Prospective trials demonstrating safety and efficacy on the target patient population
  3. Human-in-the-loop oversight — Qualified healthcare professionals must review and interpret all AI predictions
  4. Bias and fairness evaluation — Subgroup analysis across demographic groups to ensure equitable performance
  5. Continuous monitoring — Post-deployment surveillance for model drift and performance degradation

AI predictions must not be used as the sole basis for medical decisions.

Consult with regulatory affairs, clinical validation teams, and your institution's IRB/ethics board before any patient-facing deployment. For guidance on responsible AI practices in healthcare, see the AWS Responsible AI documentation and AWS Healthcare AI compliance resources.

docs.title: 1. Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone <repository-url>
cd Kiro-ML-model

docs.title: 2. Create a virtual environment
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: 3. Install dependencies
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt

This installs FastAPI, boto3, PyTorch, MONAI, MLflow, and all other required packages.

docs.title: 4. Copy environment files
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
cp .env.local.example .env.local

Edit both files with your configuration (see Configuration below).

docs.title: Quick Setup
docs.text:
Once .env.local is configured with your AWS_ACCOUNT_ID, run the setup script to create the SageMaker IAM role and build/push all Docker images in one step:

./setup.sh

Or run individual steps:

./setup.sh --role    # Only create the SageMaker execution role
./setup.sh --images  # Only build and push Docker images

The role creation script (create-sagemaker-role.sh) mirrors the Python get_or_create_role() utility from utils.py. It creates a role named AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm with the same managed policies and inline MLflow policy, so the behavior is identical whether you run the bash script or use the Python helper in notebooks.

# Equivalent standalone usage:
./create-sagemaker-role.sh                          # Uses default name
./create-sagemaker-role.sh MyCustomRoleName         # Custom name

The setup script reads all account-specific values from .env.local — no positional arguments needed.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The application loads environment variables in two layers:

  1. .env — General application configuration (loaded first)
  2. .env.local — Account-specific overrides (loaded second, takes priority)

.env.local is gitignored and should never be committed — it contains your AWS account-specific values.

docs.title: .env — General config
docs.text: Variable Description Default AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS access key (optional if using ~/.aws/credentials) — AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS secret key (optional if using ~/.aws/credentials) — AWS_DEFAULT_REGION AWS region for all services us-east-1 MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI MLflow server URI for experiment tracking http://localhost:5000 MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_NAME Default MLflow experiment name medical_imaging_experiments TENSORBOARD_LOG_DIR Directory for TensorBoard log files ./logs/tensorboard

docs.title: .env.local — Account-specific config
docs.text:
Variable Description Example AWS_ACCOUNT_ID Your 12-digit AWS account ID 123456789012 SAGEMAKER_ROLE_ARN IAM role ARN that SageMaker assumes for training and deployment arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-sgm TRAINING_IMAGE_CLASSIFICATION ECR URI for the classification training container 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-training-byoc-classification:latest TRAINING_IMAGE_SEGMENTATION ECR URI for the segmentation training container 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-training-byoc-segmentation:latest INFERENCE_IMAGE_CLASSIFICATION ECR URI for the classification inference container 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-classification:latest INFERENCE_IMAGE_SEGMENTATION ECR URI for the segmentation inference container 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/sm-inference-byoc-segmentation:latest DEFAULT_DATA_S3_URI Default S3 URI for training data (pre-populates the UI form) s3://your-bucket/training-data/ TEST_IMAGE_S3_URI S3 URI of a test DICOM image for integration tests s3://your-bucket/test/image.dcm TEST_SEGMENTATION_S3_URI S3 URI of a test NIfTI volume for segmentation tests s3://your-bucket/test/volume.nii.gz

Tip: You only need AWS_ACCOUNT_ID and SAGEMAKER_ROLE_ARN to get started. The ECR image URIs are required when launching SageMaker training jobs or deploying endpoints.

docs.title: First Launch
docs.text:
Start the application:

python main.py

The dashboard starts at http://localhost:8000.

Open it in your browser — you'll see the main dashboard with tabs for Training, Deployment, Inference, Monitoring, and more.

On first launch with empty data stores, the local job and deployment lists will be empty. See the Initial Setup section below to populate them from AWS.

docs.title: Option A: Configure AWS via environment variables
docs.text: If your .env or ~/.aws/credentials already has valid AWS credentials, the app connects automatically on startup.

docs.title: Option B: Configure AWS via the UI
docs.text:
1. Open http://localhost:8000
  2. Navigate to the AWS section
  3. Enter your Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, and Region
  4. Click Connect

docs.title: Sync existing resources from AWS
docs.text:
Once connected, pull your existing SageMaker resources into the dashboard:

  1. Go to the Training tab → click Sync from AWS to import existing training jobs
  2. Go to the Deployment tab → click Sync from AWS to import existing endpoints
  3. Go to the Evaluation tab → click Sync from AWS to import existing evaluation jobs

This populates the local data stores (data/sagemaker_jobs.json, data/deployments.json) so subsequent loads are fast and don't require AWS calls.

docs.title: Docker Setup
docs.text:
For a full development environment with MLflow and TensorBoard, use Docker Compose:

docker-compose up --build

This starts three services:

Service URL Purpose Dashboard http://localhost:8000 Main application UI and API MLflow http://localhost:5000 Experiment tracking and model registry TensorBoard http://localhost:6006 Training visualization

Alternatively, use the startup script to run all services without Docker:

chmod +x start.sh
./start.sh

This starts MLflow, TensorBoard, and the FastAPI app together in the background.

docs.title: Quick Start Workflow
docs.text: Here's a complete end-to-end workflow: connect to AWS, prepare data, train a model, deploy it, and run inference.

docs.title: Step 1 — Connect to AWS
docs.text: Ensure your AWS credentials are configured (via .env, environment variables, or the UI). Verify the connection by browsing S3 buckets in the AWS tab.

docs.title: Step 2 — Prepare training data in S3
docs.text:
Upload your medical imaging dataset to S3 in the expected folder structure:

s3://your-bucket/training-data/
├── class_a/
│   ├── image001.dcm
│   ├── image002.dcm
│   └── ...
├── class_b/
│   ├── image003.dcm
│   └── ...
└── class_c/
    └── ...

Each subfolder name becomes a class label. The number of classes is determined automatically from the folder structure.

For segmentation tasks, organize data with paired images and labels.

docs.title: Option A: SageMaker training (recommended for GPU workloads)
docs.text:
1. Go to the Training tab
  2. Select SageMaker Training
  3. Configure:
  4. Model architecture — ResNet50, VGG16, EfficientNet, DenseNet121, ViT, or custom
  5. Data S3 URI — path to your training data (pre-filled from DEFAULT_DATA_S3_URI)
  6. Instance type — e.g. ml.g5.xlarge for GPU training
  7. Epochs, learning rate, batch size — training hyperparameters
  8. MLflow tracking URI — optional, for experiment tracking
  9. Click Start Training

The job runs on SageMaker. Monitor progress in the Training tab — active jobs auto-refresh their status.

docs.title: Option B: Local training
docs.text:
1. Select Local Training in the Training tab
  2. Choose your model and dataset
  3. Training runs on your local machine with MLflow and TensorBoard tracking

docs.title: Step 4 — Deploy the model
docs.text:
Once training completes:

  1. Go to the Deployment tab
  2. Click Deploy on a completed training job, or create a new deployment:
  3. Endpoint type — choose Real-time or Async (radio buttons)
  4. Model artifacts — S3 URI of the model.tar.gz produced by training
  5. Inference image — ECR URI of the inference container (from .env.local)
  6. Instance type — e.g. ml.g5.xlarge
  7. Role ARN — SageMaker execution role (from .env.local)
  8. Output S3 URI — S3 prefix for inference results (required for async, optional for real-time)
  9. Click Deploy

The endpoint progresses from Creating → InService. This typically takes 5–10 minutes.

Once deployed, endpoint cards display scaling controls: Scale up (+), Scale down (-), and Scale to 0 (async only — real-time endpoints require a minimum of 1 instance). An active endpoint count badge shows endpoint names and instance counts at a glance.

docs.title: Step 5 — Run inference
docs.text:
Once the endpoint is InService:

  1. Go to the Inference tab
  2. Select the endpoint and task type (classification or segmentation)
  3. Provide input:
  4. S3 URI — point to an image in S3
  5. File upload — upload a DICOM or NIfTI file directly from your browser
  6. Click Invoke

The response shows predicted classes with confidence scores (classification) or a binary mask with volume statistics (segmentation).

docs.title: Step 6 — Monitor (optional)
docs.text:
Set up Model Monitor to track prediction drift:

  1. Enable Data Capture on the endpoint (Monitoring tab → Data Capture)
  2. Run a Baseline job against your training data
  3. Create a Monitoring Schedule to compare live traffic against the baseline

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Evaluation — run a SageMaker Processing Job to evaluate endpoint accuracy on a labeled test set
  • Fairness Analysis — scan DICOM metadata for demographic distributions and bias auditing
  • Fine-tuning — resume training from a checkpoint using checkpoint_s3_uri
  • Report Generation — generate academic paper sections from completed training and evaluation jobs
  • Custom Containers — build and push BYOC training/inference images (see README for build_and_push.sh instructions)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Solution ValueError: AWS credentials not configured Set credentials in .env, environment, or ~/.aws/credentials SageMaker job fails immediately Check that SAGEMAKER_ROLE_ARN has the necessary permissions (run ./create-sagemaker-role.sh to create/fix it) and the ECR image URI is correct Endpoint stuck in Creating Wait up to 10 minutes; check the SageMaker console for errors MLflow not tracking Ensure MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI points to a running MLflow server (or use Docker Compose) Docker build fails with 403 Forbidden Run aws ecr get-login-password to authenticate with the AWS Deep Learning Containers ECR (see README) SageMaker rejects image with Unsupported manifest media type Your Docker image was built in OCI format. Rebuild with docker buildx build --provenance=false or use the provided build_and_push.sh scripts which handle this automatically Real-time endpoint times out on first request This is a cold start — the model loads into GPU memory on the first invocation. The first request may exceed the 60s API gateway timeout, but subsequent requests are fast (<30s). Send a warm-up request after deployment, or use async endpoints for segmentation which have no timeout limit Real-time works on second request but not first Cold start. The model and MONAI transforms are initialized on the first predict_fn call. After that, the model stays in GPU memory and subsequent requests are fast Empty job list after restart Data stores auto-rebuild from data/training_reports/ on first boot; click Sync from AWS to pull fresh data
