Clinical deployment requires regulatory review, validation against clinical standards, and human oversight. AI predictions must not be used as the sole basis for medical decisions.

This guide covers the end-to-end workflow for training, deploying, and monitoring medical image classification and segmentation models using the MedML Training Dashboard.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Dashboard running at http://localhost:8000 (see Getting Started for setup)
  • AWS credentials configured (environment variables or entered via the dashboard)
  • S3 bucket with training data uploaded
  • SageMaker execution role ARN with appropriate permissions

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: Guide Description Training Launch local or SageMaker training jobs for classification and segmentation models Deployment Deploy trained models to SageMaker real-time or async endpoints Inference Invoke deployed endpoints with DICOM, NIfTI, or image files Evaluation Run evaluation processing jobs against deployed endpoints Monitoring Enable data capture, compute baselines, and schedule drift monitoring Fairness Analysis Scan DICOM metadata for demographic distributions and bias auditing Report Generation Generate structured academic paper sections from completed jobs

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
1. Connect to AWS — Enter credentials or rely on environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION)
  2. Upload data to S3 — Organize training data in the expected folder structure
  3. Train a model — Launch a SageMaker training job from the Training tab
  4. Deploy the model — Deploy the resulting model.tar.gz to a SageMaker endpoint
  5. Test inference — Invoke the endpoint with a sample image
  6. Evaluate — Run a full evaluation job against a labeled test set
  7. Monitor — Enable data capture and set up drift monitoring schedules
  8. Audit fairness — Scan your DICOM dataset for demographic imbalances
  9. Generate report — Produce paper sections summarizing your experiment

docs.title: Deployment Guide
docs.text:
⚠️ Research Use Only — Models trained and deployed through this platform are for research and development purposes. Clinical deployment requires regulatory review, validation against clinical standards, and human oversight. AI predictions must not be used as the sole basis for medical decisions.

This guide covers deploying trained models to SageMaker endpoints for real-time or asynchronous inference.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A completed training job with a model.tar.gz artifact in S3
  • An inference container image pushed to ECR (classification or segmentation)
  • A SageMaker execution role with endpoint creation permissions

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the Deployment tab
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:8000 and click the Deployment tab.

docs.title: Step 2 — Fill out the deploy form
docs.text: Field Description Example Endpoint Name Unique name for the endpoint spine-classifier-v2 Endpoint Type Radio button: Real-time or Async Real-time Model Artifacts S3 URI of model.tar.gz s3://bucket/output/job/output/model.tar.gz Inference Image URI ECR URI of the inference container from .env.local Role ARN SageMaker execution role from .env.local Instance Type Endpoint instance type ml.g5.xlarge Output S3 URI S3 prefix for inference results (required for async, optional for real-time) s3://bucket/async-output/

docs.title: Step 3 — Submit
docs.text:
Click Deploy. The dashboard creates three AWS resources in sequence: 1. SageMaker Model 2. Endpoint Configuration 3. Endpoint

Status transitions: Creating → InService (or Failed).

docs.title: Step 4 — Wait for InService
docs.text: The deployment list auto-refreshes status from AWS. Once the endpoint shows InService, it is ready to receive inference requests.

docs.title: Real-Time vs Async Endpoints
docs.text: The deploy form presents a radio button to choose between endpoint types:

docs.title: Real-time
docs.text:
• Synchronous request/response
  • Best for classification (fast, <5s) and pre-warmed segmentation
  • API gateway timeout: 60 seconds — requests exceeding this fail regardless of container timeout
  • Minimum 1 instance (cannot scale to zero)

Cold start warning: The first request to a real-time endpoint after deployment (or after a period of inactivity) may time out. This is because the model loads into GPU memory on the first invocation. Subsequent requests are fast (<30s). To avoid cold-start timeouts: - Send a warm-up request immediately after the endpoint becomes InService - Or use async endpoints for segmentation, which have no timeout limit

Both real-time and async endpoints use the same container and inference code. The only difference is the timeout behavior.

Recommendation: - Classification → Real-time (fast inference, <5s) - Segmentation → Async (no timeout limit, supports scale-to-zero for cost savings)

docs.title: Async endpoint
docs.text:
Select the Async radio button to create an asynchronous endpoint:

Field Required Description Output S3 URI yes S3 prefix where results are written max_concurrent no Max concurrent invocations per instance (default 10)

Async endpoints are useful for: - 3D segmentation volumes (inference takes 15-30s, first request may take longer) - Batch inference workloads - Cost optimization (scale to zero when idle — no billing when no requests)

docs.title: Endpoint Scaling
docs.text:
Each deployed endpoint card displays scaling controls:

Button Action Availability Scale up (+) Adds one instance All endpoints Scale down (-) Removes one instance (minimum 1 for real-time) All endpoints Scale to 0 Removes all instances (endpoint remains configured) Async only

Real-time endpoints require at least 1 instance and cannot be scaled to zero. Async endpoints support scaling to zero — they automatically wake up when new requests arrive.

docs.title: Active Endpoint Badge
docs.text: The deployment tab header displays a count badge showing currently active endpoints. Hovering or clicking reveals endpoint names and their instance counts, providing a quick overview of deployed resources.

docs.title: Enable Data Capture at Deploy Time
docs.text:
Check Enable Data Capture before deploying to record all inference traffic from the first request:

Field Description Enable Data Capture Check to activate Capture S3 URI S3 prefix for captured traffic (e.g. s3://bucket/capture/) Capture Sampling % Percentage of requests to capture (1-100, default 100)

This is equivalent to calling the monitoring data-capture API separately, but happens atomically during deployment.

docs.title: Import an Existing Endpoint
docs.text:
To track an endpoint that was created outside the dashboard (e.g. via the AWS console or CLI):

  1. Click Import Endpoint (or call POST /api/deployment with only the endpoint name)
  2. Omit model_artifacts — the dashboard registers the endpoint without creating a new artifact
  3. The endpoint appears in the deployment list and its status is polled from AWS

docs.title: Sync from AWS
docs.text:
Click Sync from AWS to pull existing endpoints from your AWS account and merge them into the local store:

  • Optional ?name_contains= filter to narrow results
  • Already-tracked endpoints have their status updated
  • New endpoints are added with minimal records

docs.title: From the dashboard
docs.text:
Click the Delete button on any endpoint in the list. This: 1. Deletes the SageMaker endpoint 2. Deletes the endpoint configuration 3. Deletes the SageMaker model resource 4. Removes the local record from data/deployments.json

The local record is always cleaned up via try/finally, even if an AWS API call fails.

docs.title: External deletion handling
docs.text: If an endpoint is deleted outside the dashboard (AWS console, CLI, etc.): - The next status poll detects the missing endpoint - The local record is marked as "Deleted" - Deleted entries are filtered out of the list response

docs.title: Model Archive Requirements
docs.text:
SageMaker's PyTorch serving container expects inference code at code/inference.py inside model.tar.gz:

model.tar.gz
├── best_model.pth
├── result.json
└── code/
    └── inference.py

Training scripts automatically copy inference artifacts to model_dir/code/ during training. If you have an older model archive with inference.py at the root, use the repackaging utility:

python tests/integration/repackage_model.py s3://your-bucket/output/job-name/output/model.tar.gz

docs.title: Security: Model Loading
docs.text: All model loading in training and evaluation code uses torch.load(path, weights_only=True) to prevent arbitrary code execution from untrusted model files. The inference script (code/inference.py) uses torch.load(path, map_location=device) without weights_only=True because it loads models produced by the project's own training pipeline — this trust boundary is documented in the code.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Cause Fix Endpoint stuck in Creating Container startup failure Check CloudWatch logs for the endpoint Failed status Missing inference script or bad model Verify model.tar.gz contains code/inference.py and best_model.pth (not inference.py at root) Permission denied Role ARN lacks permissions Ensure the role has sagemaker:CreateEndpoint, ecr:GetAuthorizationToken, s3:GetObject Timeout on invocation Model too large or slow Increase instance type or use async endpoint

docs.title: Evaluation Guide
docs.text: This guide covers running SageMaker Processing Jobs to evaluate deployed classification endpoints against labeled test sets.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A deployed classification endpoint in InService status
  • A labeled test dataset in S3 organized by class folders
  • A SageMaker execution role with processing job permissions

docs.title: Test Data Format
docs.text:
Organize your test data in S3 with one subfolder per class:

s3://your-bucket/test-data/
├── class_a/
│   ├── image001.dcm
│   ├── image002.dcm
│   └── image003.dcm
├── class_b/
│   ├── image004.dcm
│   └── image005.dcm
└── class_c/
    ├── image006.dcm
    └── image007.dcm

Each subfolder name is used as the ground-truth label.

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the Evaluation tab
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:8000 and click the Evaluation tab.

docs.title: Step 2 — Fill out the evaluation form
docs.text: Field Required Description Example Endpoint Name Yes The deployed endpoint to evaluate spine-classifier-v2 Test Data S3 URI Yes S3 path to the labeled test dataset s3://bucket/test-data/ Output S3 URI Yes S3 prefix where results are written s3://bucket/eval-output/ Processing Image URI Yes ECR URI of the processing container Same as inference image Role ARN Yes SageMaker execution role from .env.local Instance Type No Processing instance type ml.m5.xlarge

docs.title: Step 3 — Submit
docs.text: Click Run Evaluation. A SageMaker Processing Job is launched that: 1. Discovers class folders under the test data URI 2. Invokes the endpoint for every file 3. Collects predictions and probability scores 4. Computes metrics and generates output artifacts

docs.title: Step 4 — Wait for completion
docs.text: The job typically takes a few minutes depending on the dataset size. Status is polled from AWS.

docs.title: Output Artifacts
docs.text:
The evaluation job writes four files to the output S3 URI:

File Description metrics.json Accuracy, macro AUC, per-class precision/recall/F1, and support counts predictions.csv Per-file ground truth vs predicted class with per-class probabilities confusion_matrix.png Confusion matrix heatmap visualization roc_auc.png ROC-AUC curves (one per class, one-vs-rest)

docs.title: metrics.json structure
docs.text:
{
  "accuracy": 0.8750,
  "macro_auc": 0.9412,
  "per_class": {
    "class_a": {
      "precision": 0.90,
      "recall": 0.85,
      "f1": 0.87,
      "support": 20
    },
    "class_b": {
      "precision": 0.82,
      "recall": 0.88,
      "f1": 0.85,
      "support": 25
    }
  }
}

docs.title: predictions.csv structure
docs.text:
file,true_class,predicted_class,prob_class_a,prob_class_b,prob_class_c
image001.dcm,class_a,class_a,0.89,0.07,0.04
image004.dcm,class_b,class_c,0.12,0.35,0.53

docs.title: Viewing Results
docs.text:
Once the evaluation job completes:

  1. The results panel shows overall accuracy and macro AUC
  2. Click on a job to view:
  3. Confusion matrix — visual heatmap of predictions vs ground truth
  4. ROC-AUC curves — per-class curves with AUC values
  5. Per-class metrics table — precision, recall, F1, support for each class
  6. Download individual artifacts for further analysis

docs.title: Endpoint Response Formats Handled
docs.text:
The evaluation script supports two endpoint response formats transparently:

Format Structure Batched arrays {"predictions": [[p0, p1, ...]], "predicted_class": [idx], "confidence": [c]} Named probabilities {"probabilities": {"class_a": 0.3, ...}, "predicted_class": "class_a"}

docs.title: Sync from AWS
docs.text: Click Sync from AWS (or POST /api/evaluation/sync) to pull evaluation processing jobs from AWS. Use ?name_contains= to filter.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use a representative test set — include edge cases and all class labels
  • Check class balance — imbalanced test sets can produce misleading accuracy; look at per-class metrics
  • Compare across runs — use the Report Generation feature to compile results from multiple jobs
  • Subgroup analysis — combine with Fairness Analysis to check if performance varies across demographic groups

docs.title: Fairness Analysis Guide
docs.text:
⚠️ Research Use Only — Models trained and deployed through this platform are for research and development purposes. Clinical deployment requires regulatory review, validation against clinical standards, and human oversight. AI predictions must not be used as the sole basis for medical decisions.

This guide covers scanning DICOM datasets for demographic distributions and identifying potential biases in your training data.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Fairness Analysis feature reads DICOM metadata from files in S3 and extracts demographic attributes to help you understand the composition of your dataset. Imbalanced demographic distributions can lead to biased model performance across patient subgroups.

docs.title: What It Extracts
docs.text:
The scanner reads the following DICOM tags from each file:

DICOM Tag Field Example Values PatientSex Sex/Gender M, F, O PatientAge Age 045Y, 6M, 2W EthnicGroup Ethnicity Varies by institution PatientRace Race Varies by institution Modality Imaging modality CT, MR, CR, DX BodyPartExamined Body part CHEST, SPINE, HEAD

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the Fairness tab
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:8000 and click the Fairness Analysis tab.

docs.title: Step 2 — Configure the scan
docs.text: Field Description Default S3 Prefix S3 path containing DICOM files (scanned recursively) — Max Files Maximum number of DICOM files to scan 200

docs.title: Step 3 — Run the scan
docs.text: Click Scan. The service: 1. Lists DICOM files under the S3 prefix 2. Downloads each file with stop_before_pixels=True (efficient — skips pixel data) 3. Extracts demographic tags from up to max_files files 4. Returns aggregated distributions

docs.title: API
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/fairness/scan \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "s3_prefix": "s3://my-bucket/training-data/",
    "max_files": 200
  }'

docs.title: Per-Attribute Value Counts
docs.text:
Shows the distribution of each demographic attribute:

PatientSex:
  M: 120 (60%)
  F: 75 (37.5%)
  O: 5 (2.5%)

Modality:
  CR: 150 (75%)
  DX: 50 (25%)

docs.title: Age Bucketing
docs.text:
DICOM age strings (045Y, 6M, 2W) are normalized to integer years and bucketed:

Bucket Age Range 0-17 Pediatric 18-29 Young adult 30-44 Adult 45-59 Middle-aged 60-74 Senior 75+ Elderly

Age format parsing: - 045Y → 45 years - 6M → 0 years (infant) - 2W → 0 years (neonate)

docs.title: Missing Rate Analysis
docs.text:
Shows the percentage of files where each tag was absent or empty:

Missing Rates:
  PatientSex: 2.5%
  PatientAge: 8.0%
  EthnicGroup: 65.0%
  PatientRace: 72.0%
  Modality: 0.0%
  BodyPartExamined: 1.5%

High missing rates for EthnicGroup and PatientRace are common — many institutions do not populate these fields.

docs.title: Sample Records
docs.text: Up to 50 file-level rows showing per-file demographic values for manual inspection.

docs.title: 1. Scan your training data
docs.text: Run a fairness scan on the S3 prefix containing your training dataset.

docs.title: 2. Identify imbalances
docs.text: Look for: - Severe skew — e.g. 90% male / 10% female - Missing subgroups — e.g. no pediatric patients - High missing rates — e.g. race data missing for 70%+ of files

docs.title: 3. Cross-reference with evaluation
docs.text: After running an evaluation job: - Compare per-class performance metrics across demographic subgroups - Check if the model underperforms on underrepresented groups

docs.title: 4. Take action
docs.text: Finding Possible Action Severe sex imbalance Collect more data from underrepresented sex Missing age groups Augment dataset or document limitation High missing rates Contact data source about completeness Performance disparity Retrain with balanced sampling or stratified splits

docs.title: 5. Include in reports
docs.text: Set include_fairness: true when generating paper reports to automatically include the fairness analysis in the Methods and Discussion sections.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only scans DICOM files (NIfTI volumes do not contain demographic metadata)
  • Relies on tags being populated by the source institution
  • EthnicGroup and PatientRace are often empty in practice
  • Max 200 files by default — increase max_files for larger datasets (trades off speed)
  • Does not compute statistical significance — use as a screening tool

docs.title: Inference Guide
docs.text: This guide covers invoking deployed SageMaker endpoints for classification and segmentation predictions.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A deployed endpoint in InService status (see Deployment Guide)
  • The endpoint's task type: classification or segmentation

docs.title: Via the Dashboard UI
docs.text:
1. Go to the Inference tab
  2. Select the endpoint from the dropdown
  3. Choose the input method:
  4. S3 URI — enter the S3 path to your file
  5. File Upload — upload a file directly from your browser
  6. Click Invoke
  7. View the response in the results panel

docs.title: Via the API — S3 URI input
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/inference/invoke \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "endpoint_name": "spine-classifier-v2",
    "task_type": "classification",
    "input_type": "s3_uri",
    "input_value": "s3://<your-bucket-name>/test/image.dcm"
  }'

docs.title: Via the API — File upload (raw bytes)
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/inference/invoke-local?endpoint_name=spine-classifier-v2&task_type=classification" \
  --data-binary @/path/to/image.dcm

docs.title: Optional: save result to S3
docs.text:
Add output_s3_uri to save the response:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/inference/invoke \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "endpoint_name": "spine-classifier-v2",
    "task_type": "classification",
    "input_type": "s3_uri",
    "input_value": "s3://<your-bucket-name>/test/image.dcm",
    "output_s3_uri": "s3://<your-bucket-name>/results/"
  }'

The result is saved to s3://<prefix>/<endpoint_name>-result.json.

docs.title: Classification endpoints
docs.text: Format How to send DICOM (.dcm) Raw bytes with Content-Type: application/dicom, or S3 URI, or base64 PNG / JPG Same as DICOM — raw bytes, S3 URI, or base64 S3 URI JSON: {"file_path": "s3://bucket/key.dcm"} Local path JSON: {"file_path": "/path/to/image.dcm"} Base64 JSON: {"file_path": "<base64-encoded bytes>"}

docs.title: Segmentation endpoints
docs.text:
Format How to send NIfTI (.nii.gz) Raw bytes with Content-Type: application/octet-stream S3 URI JSON: {"file_path": "s3://bucket/subject/img.nii.gz"} Local path JSON: {"file_path": "/path/to/volume.nii.gz"} Base64 JSON: {"file_path": "<base64-encoded NIfTI bytes>"}

Note: The segmentation inference script uses the file_path key (same as classification). The older s3_uri key is no longer used — always use file_path for both task types.

docs.title: Classification
docs.text:
{
  "predictions": [[0.1034, 0.1202, 0.1366, 0.0866, 0.1258, 0.1408, 0.1155, 0.1713]],
  "predicted_class": [7],
  "confidence": [0.1713]
}
Field Type Description predictions list[list[float]] Probability array per input (batched) predicted_class list[int] Index of the highest-probability class confidence list[float] Probability of the predicted class

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text:
{
  "mask_nifti_b64": "<base64-encoded .nii.gz bytes>",
  "shape": [128, 128, 64],
  "voxels_positive": 14823,
  "voxels_total": 1048576,
  "volume_fraction": 0.0141
}
Field Type Description mask_nifti_b64 string Base64-encoded binary mask as a NIfTI file shape list[int] Dimensions of the output mask voxels_positive int Number of positive (foreground) voxels voxels_total int Total voxels in the mask volume_fraction float Ratio of positive voxels to total

The segmentation inference pipeline uses SlidingWindowInferer for memory-efficient processing of large 3D volumes, with Orientation and Spacing transforms applied to normalize inputs before prediction. This ensures consistent results regardless of the input volume's original orientation or voxel spacing.

To save the segmentation mask locally:

import base64

mask_bytes = base64.b64decode(response["mask_nifti_b64"])
with open("mask.nii.gz", "wb") as f:
    f.write(mask_bytes)

docs.title: Async Endpoint Inference
docs.text:
When invoking an endpoint, the dashboard automatically detects whether the target is a real-time or async endpoint and adjusts the invocation method accordingly:

  • Real-time endpoints — sends a synchronous InvokeEndpoint request and returns the response immediately
  • Async endpoints — sends an InvokeEndpointAsync request, which returns an output location in S3 where the result will be written

No additional configuration is needed in the inference UI — select the endpoint and invoke as normal. The dashboard handles the async/real-time distinction transparently.

For async endpoints, the result panel shows the S3 output location and polls for completion automatically.

docs.title: CLI Tools
docs.text: For quick testing without the dashboard:

docs.title: Classification
docs.text:
python tests/invoke_endpoint.py --s3-uri s3://bucket/image.dcm --endpoint my-endpoint
python tests/invoke_endpoint.py --image /path/to/image.dcm --endpoint my-endpoint

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text:
python test_endpoint_segmentation.py --endpoint my-seg-endpoint \
    --s3-uri s3://bucket/subject/img.nii.gz

python test_endpoint_segmentation.py --endpoint my-seg-endpoint \
    --local /path/to/volume.nii.gz

python test_endpoint_segmentation.py --endpoint my-seg-endpoint \
    --s3-uri s3://bucket/img.nii.gz --save-mask /tmp/mask.nii.gz

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Cause Fix Empty mask (0 positive voxels) Input outside expected HU range Check that input is CT data in [-100, 500] HU range ModelError Inference script crash Check CloudWatch logs for the endpoint Timeout Volume too large Use async endpoint or a larger instance type ValidationException Endpoint not InService Wait for deployment to complete or check for failures

docs.title: Monitoring Guide
docs.text:
⚠️ Research Use Only — Models trained and deployed through this platform are for research and development purposes. Clinical deployment requires regulatory review, validation against clinical standards, and human oversight. AI predictions must not be used as the sole basis for medical decisions.

This guide covers the full SageMaker Model Monitor lifecycle: data capture, traffic analysis, baselines, and monitoring schedules.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Model monitoring detects data quality drift and prediction drift on deployed endpoints. The workflow is:

  1. Enable data capture — record inference requests and responses to S3
  2. View captured traffic — analyze prediction distributions and confidence scores
  3. Run a data quality baseline — compute reference statistics from training data
  4. Create a monitoring schedule — automatically compare live traffic against the baseline

docs.title: Step 1 — Enable Data Capture
docs.text: Data capture records every inference request and response as .jsonl files in S3.

docs.title: Option A: At deploy time (recommended)
docs.text:
When deploying an endpoint, check Enable Data Capture in the form: - Capture S3 URI — e.g. s3://your-bucket/capture/ - Capture Sampling % — percentage of requests to capture (1-100, default 100)

Capture is active from the first inference call.

docs.title: Option B: After deployment
docs.text:
1. Go to Monitoring → Data Capture
  2. Select the endpoint from the dropdown
  3. Enter the Capture S3 URI (root prefix only, e.g. s3://your-bucket/capture/)
  4. Set the Sampling Percentage (default 100)
  5. Click Enable

SageMaker updates the endpoint in-place (status shows Updating for a few minutes).

docs.title: API
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/monitoring/data-capture \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "endpoint_name": "spine-classifier-v2",
    "capture_s3_uri": "s3://my-bucket/capture/",
    "sampling_percentage": 100
  }'

docs.title: S3 path structure
docs.text:
SageMaker writes captured data to: 

s3://your-bucket/capture/<endpoint-name>/AllTraffic/<year>/<month>/<day>/<hour>/

Enter the root prefix only — not the full dated path.

docs.title: Step 2 — View Captured Traffic (Capture Viewer)
docs.text:
After making inference calls, analyze the captured traffic:

  1. Go to Monitoring → Capture Viewer
  2. Select the endpoint from the dropdown — the Capture S3 URI auto-fills if capture was enabled via the dashboard
  3. Set Max Files (default 20)
  4. Click Analyse

docs.title: What the viewer shows
docs.text:
• Summary cards — total records, files scanned, average confidence, classes seen
  • Prediction class distribution — bar chart of predicted classes
  • Confidence score histogram — 10-bucket histogram of confidence values
  • Recent captures table — up to 50 rows with per-prediction probabilities

docs.title: API
docs.text:
curl "http://localhost:8000/api/monitoring/capture-summary?endpoint_name=spine-classifier-v2&capture_s3_uri=s3://bucket/capture/&max_files=20"

Returns: 

{
  "class_distribution": {"0": 15, "1": 8, "2": 12},
  "confidence_histogram": [0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 5, 8, 10, 6, 0],
  "avg_confidence": 0.72,
  "recent_records": []
}

docs.title: Step 3 — Run a Data Quality Baseline
docs.text:
A baseline computes statistics and constraints from a reference dataset (typically your training data). These are used by monitoring schedules to detect drift.

  1. Go to Monitoring → Data Quality Baseline
  2. Fill in the form:
Field Description Example Baseline Data S3 URI S3 path to your reference dataset s3://bucket/training-data/ Output S3 URI Where constraints and statistics are written s3://bucket/baseline-output/ IAM Role ARN SageMaker execution role from .env.local Instance Type Processing instance ml.m5.xlarge Job Name (Optional) Custom name spine-baseline-v1
  1. Click Run Baseline Job

The job submits a SageMaker Processing Job using the prebuilt Model Monitor container. Once complete, the baseline card shows S3 paths for: - constraints.json - statistics.json

Click "Use in Schedule" to auto-fill the monitoring schedule form with these paths.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/monitoring/baseline/data-quality \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "baseline_data_s3_uri": "s3://bucket/training-data/",
    "output_s3_uri": "s3://bucket/baseline-output/",
    "role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerRole"
  }'

docs.title: Data Quality Schedule
docs.text:
Monitors for data drift by comparing captured traffic against baseline constraints.

  1. Go to Monitoring → Data Quality Schedule
  2. Fill in the form:
Field Description Example Schedule Name Unique name spine-data-quality-hourly Endpoint Name Endpoint to monitor spine-classifier-v2 Constraints S3 URI From baseline output auto-filled from baseline Statistics S3 URI From baseline output auto-filled from baseline Output S3 URI Where violation reports go s3://bucket/monitoring-output/ Schedule Expression Cron or rate expression cron(0 * ? * * *) (hourly)
  1. Click Create Schedule

docs.title: Model Quality Schedule
docs.text:
Monitors prediction quality by comparing endpoint predictions against ground-truth labels in S3.

  1. Go to Monitoring → Model Quality Schedule
  2. Fill in the form:
Field Description Example Schedule Name Unique name spine-model-quality-daily Endpoint Name Endpoint to monitor spine-classifier-v2 Problem Type Classification type MulticlassClassification Ground Truth S3 URI S3 path to labels s3://bucket/ground-truth/ Inference Attribute Response field for prediction predicted_class Probability Attribute (Optional) Probability field confidence Output S3 URI Where reports go s3://bucket/model-quality-output/ Schedule Expression Cron or rate rate(1 day)
  1. Click Create Schedule

Supported problem types: BinaryClassification, MulticlassClassification, Regression.

docs.title: List all schedules
docs.text:
Go to Monitoring → Schedules or call:

curl http://localhost:8000/api/monitoring/schedules

Schedules are sorted by creation time (newest first). Active schedules are refreshed from AWS.

Pass ?local_only=true to skip the AWS refresh.

docs.title: Refresh a schedule
docs.text:
Click Refresh on a schedule card to pull the latest status and most recent execution summary (status, time, Processing Job ARN, failure reason).

curl http://localhost:8000/api/monitoring/schedules/spine-data-quality-hourly

docs.title: Delete a schedule
docs.text:
Click Delete to stop and delete the monitoring schedule from AWS and remove it from the local store.

curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8000/api/monitoring/schedules/spine-data-quality-hourly

docs.title: Schedule Expressions
docs.text: Expression Meaning cron(0 * ? * * *) Every hour at minute 0 cron(0 0 ? * * *) Daily at midnight cron(0 0 ? * MON *) Every Monday at midnight rate(1 hour) Every hour rate(1 day) Every day

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Cause Fix No capture files found Capture not yet enabled or no invocations made Enable capture and invoke the endpoint Baseline job fails Insufficient permissions or bad data path Check the Processing Job logs in CloudWatch Schedule shows no executions Not enough time elapsed or no captured data Wait for the next scheduled run; ensure data capture is working

docs.title: Report Generation Guide
docs.text:
⚠️ Research Use Only — Models trained and deployed through this platform are for research and development purposes. Clinical deployment requires regulatory review, validation against clinical standards, and human oversight. AI predictions must not be used as the sole basis for medical decisions.

This guide covers generating structured academic paper sections from completed training and evaluation jobs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Report Generation feature produces formatted sections for research papers and technical reports based on your experiment data. It pulls metrics, hyperparameters, and results from completed jobs and structures them into standard academic sections.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• At least one completed (non-archived) training job
  • (Optional) Completed evaluation jobs with metrics
  • (Optional) Fairness analysis results

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the Report tab
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:8000 and click the Report tab.

docs.title: Step 2 — Select jobs
docs.text:
The job list shows only eligible jobs: - Training jobs — completed, non-archived - Evaluation jobs — completed

Select one or more training jobs and evaluation jobs to include.

docs.title: Step 3 — Configure the report
docs.text: Field Description Example Title Study/paper title "Spine X-ray Classification with DenseNet121" Sections Which sections to generate abstract, methods, results, discussion Include Fairness Include fairness analysis true / false

docs.title: Step 4 — Generate
docs.text: Click Generate Report. The service compiles data from the selected jobs and produces the requested sections.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/report/generate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Spine X-ray Classification with DenseNet121",
    "training_job_names": ["spine-densenet-v1", "spine-densenet-v2"],
    "evaluation_job_names": ["eval-spine-v2"],
    "sections": ["abstract", "methods", "results", "discussion"],
    "include_fairness": true
  }'

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: A concise summary of the study including: - Task description - Model architecture and key hyperparameters - Dataset summary - Main results (accuracy, AUC)

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Detailed methodology including: - Model architecture and configuration - Training setup (epochs, batch size, learning rate, instance type) - Data source and preprocessing - Evaluation protocol - Fairness analysis methodology (if include_fairness: true)

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Quantitative results including: - Training metrics (final train/val accuracy, loss) - Evaluation metrics (accuracy, macro AUC, per-class F1) - Comparison across multiple runs (if multiple jobs selected) - Fairness findings (if included)

docs.title: Discussion
docs.text: Interpretation of results including: - Performance analysis - Comparison between model variants (if multiple jobs) - Limitations - Fairness implications (if included)

docs.title: List Available Jobs
docs.text:
To see which jobs are eligible for report generation:

curl http://localhost:8000/api/report/jobs

Returns only: - Completed, non-archived training jobs - Completed evaluation jobs

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Select related jobs — compare variants of the same model or different architectures on the same dataset
  • Include evaluation — reports are richer when evaluation metrics are available
  • Enable fairness — adds demographic distribution discussion to Methods and any performance disparities to Discussion
  • Use multiple training jobs — the report can compare hyperparameter choices and their impact on performance

docs.title: Training Guide
docs.text: This guide covers launching classification and segmentation training jobs — both locally and on SageMaker.

docs.title: Classification
docs.text: Model Notes ResNet50 General-purpose CNN, good baseline VGG16 Classic architecture, larger memory footprint EfficientNet Best accuracy/compute trade-off DenseNet121 Dense connections, good for small datasets ViT Vision Transformer, requires more data Custom Upload your own model_def.py

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text: Model Notes SegResNet MONAI's residual encoder-decoder, fast training SwinUNETR Transformer-based, state-of-the-art for 3D UNet Classic encoder-decoder architecture

docs.title: Data Format
docs.text: Upload your training data to S3 in the following structure:

docs.title: Classification
docs.text:
s3://your-bucket/dataset-name/
├── train/
│   ├── class_a/
│   │   ├── image001.dcm
│   │   └── image002.dcm
│   └── class_b/
│       ├── image003.dcm
│       └── image004.dcm
├── val/
│   ├── class_a/
│   └── class_b/
└── test/        (optional — used for evaluation)
    ├── class_a/
    └── class_b/
  • Each subfolder name becomes a class label
  • num_classes is derived automatically from the folder structure
  • Supported file formats: DICOM (.dcm), PNG, JPG, NIfTI

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text:
s3://your-bucket/dataset-name/
├── train/
│   ├── subject_001/
│   │   ├── img.nii.gz
│   │   └── mask.nii.gz
│   └── subject_002/
│       ├── img.nii.gz
│       └── mask.nii.gz
└── val/
    ├── subject_003/
    └── subject_004/
  • Each subject folder contains an image volume and a binary mask
  • Output is always 1 channel (binary segmentation)

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the Training tab
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:8000 and click the Training tab.

docs.title: Step 2 — Fill out the training form
docs.text:
Task Type and Dimension (2D/3D) appear at the top of the form — selecting these first determines which model architectures and configuration options are shown below.

Field Description Example Task Type classification or segmentation (top of form) classification Dimension 2D or 3D (top of form, determines model options) 2D Data S3 URI S3 path to your dataset root s3://my-bucket/spine-xray/ Model Architecture to train DenseNet121 Epochs Number of training epochs 50 Batch Size Mini-batch size 16 Learning Rate Initial learning rate 0.0001 Instance Type SageMaker instance ml.g5.xlarge Training Image URI ECR URI of the BYOC container from .env.local Role ARN SageMaker execution role from .env.local MLflow Tracking URI (Optional) MLflow server URL http://your-mlflow:5000

docs.title: Step 3 — Submit
docs.text: Click Start Training. The job appears in the Active tab with status InProgress.

docs.title: Step 4 — Monitor progress
docs.text:
• The job list auto-refreshes status from AWS for active jobs
  • Once complete, the job moves to the Completed tab with billable seconds and estimated cost

docs.title: MLflow Integration
docs.text:
To enable experiment tracking:

  1. Set the MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI environment variable (in .env or the training form)
  2. The training script automatically logs:
  3. Hyperparameters (model, epochs, learning rate, batch size)
  4. Per-epoch metrics (train loss, train accuracy, val accuracy, val loss)
  5. Best model checkpoint as an artifact
  6. result.json with training provenance

For SageMaker-managed MLflow tracking servers, use the dashboard's presigned URL feature to get a temporary access URL.

docs.title: Fine-Tuning from a Previous Job
docs.text:
To continue training from a completed job's checkpoint:

  1. Find the completed job's model artifact S3 URI (e.g. s3://bucket/output/job-name/output/model.tar.gz)
  2. In the training form, set Checkpoint S3 URI to that path
  3. The training script will:
  4. Download and extract the archive
  5. Load best_model.pth (or model.pth) — restoring model weights and optimizer state
  6. Set start_epoch to the checkpoint's epoch + 1
  7. Record the source URI in result.json under fine_tuned_from

If the checkpoint cannot be loaded, training falls back to starting from scratch with a warning.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text: Tab Shows Active Jobs in InProgress or Stopping state Completed Successfully finished jobs Failed Jobs that errored out Archived Jobs you've hidden from the default view

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Action Description Sync from AWS Pull up to 100 jobs from AWS and merge into local store. Use ?name_contains= to filter. Archive Hide a job from the default list (still accessible in the Archived tab) Comment Attach a free-text note to any job Delete Artifacts Delete model.tar.gz from S3 and mark the job as artifacts_deleted Remove Delete a job from local tracking (only allowed when not active) Fetch Result Download result.json from the model artifact (reconstructs if missing)

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Use the search bar to filter jobs by name. The ?name_contains= query parameter also works with the Sync from AWS operation to pull only matching jobs.

docs.title: Custom Models
docs.text: To use a custom architecture:

docs.title: Step 1 — Create your model code
docs.text:
Create a zip file containing at minimum a model_def.py with a get_model(num_classes) function:

# model_def.py
import torch.nn as nn
from torchvision import models

def get_model(num_classes):
    model = models.resnet18(pretrained=True)
    model.fc = nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, num_classes)
    return model

docs.title: Step 2 — Upload the zip
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/training/models/upload-code?model_name=my_custom_model" \
  -F "file=@my_model.zip"

Or use the dashboard's Upload Custom Model form.

docs.title: Step 3 — Select in training form
docs.text: Choose your custom model from the model dropdown when launching a job. The code is extracted to data/custom_models/<model_name>/ and bundled into the training container.

docs.title: Local Training
docs.text:
For quick experiments without SageMaker:

  1. Select Local as the training target
  2. Fill in the same form fields (data path can be local or S3)
  3. Training runs on the dashboard server with MLflow and TensorBoard tracking
  4. Results appear in the local training history

Local training is useful for prototyping but limited by the server's hardware. Use SageMaker for GPU-accelerated training on larger datasets.
